title: Grandma-Style Soft Sourdough Sandwich Bread
description: Description A soft, fluffy homemade sourdough sandwich loaf with a tender crumb and a golden crust. Made with all-purpose flour, olive oil, honey, and active sourdough starter. This is a slow-rising, overnight bread with a wonderful homemade flavour. Perfect for sandwiches, toast, and buttered slices. Yield: 1 large loaf Preparation: Day 1 and Day 2 Oven: 375°F (190°C) Pan: 9 × 5-inch loaf pan ---
ingredients:
To Prepare ¼ Cup (50 g) Active Sourdough Starter
- 2 teaspoons (10 g) sourdough starter
- 3 tablespoons (25 g) all-purpose flour
- 5 teaspoons (25 g) water
Bread Dough
- ¼ cup (50 g) active sourdough starter
- 1 cup + 2½ tablespoons (275 g) water
- 4 tablespoons (60 g) olive oil
- 1 tablespoon honey
- 4 cups + 2 tablespoons (500 g) all-purpose flour
- 2 teaspoons (10 g) sea salt
You may substitute maple syrup or sugar for the honey.
---
directions:
DAY 1 – Prepare the Starter and Mix the Dough
7:00 AM – Feed the Starter
1. Place 2 teaspoons of sourdough starter in a clean jar.
2. Add the flour and water.
3. Stir until everything is well combined.
4. Cover loosely and leave at room temperature, ideally 68–72°F (20–22°C).
5. Allow the starter to rise until doubled in size and bubbly. This usually takes about 12 hours.
The starter should look airy, active, and slightly domed before using.
7:00 PM – Mix the Dough
1. Place the active starter, water, olive oil, and honey in a large mixing bowl.
2. Stir until combined.
3. Add the flour and salt.
4. Mix with a sturdy spoon or dough whisk until a rough, shaggy dough forms.
5. Use your hands to bring together any remaining dry flour.
6. Cover the bowl and let the dough rest for 1 hour.
This resting period allows the flour to absorb the moisture and makes kneading easier.
8:00 PM – Knead and Begin the First Rise
1. Fit a stand mixer with the dough hook.
2. Knead on low speed for 8–10 minutes.
3. The dough should become smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky. It should pull away from the sides of the bowl.
4. If kneading by hand, work the dough on a lightly oiled surface until smooth and elastic.
5. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl.
6. Cover well and leave at room temperature overnight.
Allow approximately 10–12 hours, or until the dough has doubled in size.
Grandma's Tip: Watch the dough rather than the clock. A cool kitchen may require more time, while a warm kitchen may make the dough rise much faster.
DAY 2 – Shape and Bake
6:00 AM – Shape the Loaf
1. Lightly flour your work surface.
2. Gently turn out the risen dough.
3. Press it into a rectangle, with the shorter end facing you.
4. Fold the left and right sides toward the centre.
5. Starting at the far end, roll the dough toward yourself into a loaf shape.
6. Gently pull the loaf toward yourself to create a little tension on the outside.
7. Pinch the seam and ends closed.
8. Place seam-side down in a greased 9 × 5-inch loaf pan.
Second Rise
1. Cover loosely with a clean towel or lightly greased plastic wrap.
2. Leave at room temperature until the dough rises approximately 1 inch above the rim of the pan.
3. This may take 2–3 hours, depending on your kitchen temperature.
The dough should look light and puffy. Avoid letting it rise so much that it begins to collapse.
9:00 AM – Bake
1. Preheat the oven to 450°F (232°C).
2. Place the loaf in the oven.
3. Immediately reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).
4. Bake for 45–50 minutes, until deeply golden brown.
5. Remove from the oven and allow the bread to rest in the pan for 10–15 minutes.
6. Turn out onto a cooling rack.
7. Let cool completely before slicing.
---
HELPFUL BAKING NOTES
Cool Kitchens – Below 68°F (20°C)
The dough may take longer to rise. For a faster fermentation, the original recipe suggests using:
- 100 g active sourdough starter
- 255 g water
Keep the remaining ingredients the same.
Warm Kitchens – Above 72°F (22°C)
The dough may rise more quickly. If it is likely to over-proof overnight, mix the dough in the morning instead and watch its progress.
If the Dough Over-Proofs
Do not throw it away! If it becomes too sticky or loses its shape, gently transfer it to a well-oiled baking pan and make sourdough focaccia.
notes:
- Keep completely cooled bread in a bread bag, beeswax wrap, or clean kitchen towel.
- Store at room temperature for a few days.
- For longer storage, slice and freeze in a freezer-safe container or bag.
---

title: Sourdough English Muffins
description: Soft, tangy sourdough muffins with a golden, cornmeal-dusted crust. Cook them on a griddle or in a skillet, then split with a fork and toast.
ingredients:
• 200 g sourdough starter
• 2 tablespoons honey
• 480 g warm milk
• 10 g salt
• 720 g bread flour
• Cornmeal, for dusting
• Flour, for shaping as needed
• Oil or nonstick spray, if cooking in a pan
directions:
1. Mix the dough: In a large bowl, whisk together the sourdough starter, honey, and warm milk. Add the salt and bread flour.
Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
2. Knead: Knead by hand for about 8–10 minutes, or with a mixer and dough hook for 5–7 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
The dough should be soft and slightly tacky; add only a little extra flour if it is unmanageably sticky.
3. First rise: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and leave at room temperature until noticeably puffy and roughly
doubled. This may take about 4–8 hours or longer depending on starter strength and room temperature.
4. Chill for easier shaping (optional): Cover and refrigerate for 30–60 minutes if the dough is very soft or sticky.
5. Shape: Lightly dust the work surface with flour. Roll the dough to about 1.5–2 cm (½–¾ inch) thick. Cut rounds with a 7.5–9
cm (3–3½ inch) cutter. Gather scraps gently and cut remaining rounds.
6. Dust and proof: Sprinkle a tray generously with cornmeal, arrange the rounds with space between them, and dust the tops
with more cornmeal. Cover and let rise until puffy, usually 1–3 hours. They may not double.
7. Cook on a griddle or in a skillet: Preheat a heavy skillet or griddle over low to medium-low heat and lightly grease it.
Cook muffins in batches for about 6–9 minutes per side, adjusting the heat so the outsides brown slowly without burning.
8. Check doneness: If the muffins brown before the centres cook, finish them in a 175°C / 350°F oven for about 5–10
minutes. The centres should be cooked through; an internal temperature around 93°C / 200°F is a useful guide.
9. Cool: Transfer to a wire rack and cool completely before splitting. For the classic texture, split with a fork and toast before
serving.
notes:
• Sourdough timing depends on the temperature of the room and how active the starter is. Watch the dough, not just the clock.
• Keep the griddle heat low: English muffins need time to cook through without scorching.
• Fork-splitting creates the traditional nooks and crannies. Store cooled muffins airtight for 2–3 days, or freeze for longer storage.
NUTRITION (ESTIMATE)
Assuming 12 muffins: approximately 290–320 calories per muffin, depending on the milk and exact flour weight. This is a
rough estimate; cutting size and final yield will change the values.

Sourdough • Breakfast • Bread • Freezer-Friendly

title: Grandma’s Homemade English Muffins
description: Soft and chewy inside, golden on the outside, with classic nooks and crannies for catching melted butter. Cooked on the stovetop for an old-fashioned homemade breakfast. Yield Total time Method 8–10 muffins 2–2½ hours Skillet / griddle
ingredients:
• 1 cup (240 mL) warm milk
• 2 tablespoons sugar
• 2¼ teaspoons instant yeast (1 packet)
• 3 tablespoons softened butter
• 1 large egg
• 3 cups (375 g) all-purpose flour, approximately
• 1 teaspoon salt
• Cornmeal, for dusting
directions:
1. Activate the yeast. Combine warm milk, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl. If using active dry yeast, let stand 5 minutes;
instant yeast can be mixed directly into the flour.
2. Make the dough. Mix in butter and egg. Gradually add flour and salt, stirring until a soft dough forms.
3. Knead. Knead by hand for 8–10 minutes or with a stand mixer for 5–7 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Add a little flour only
if excessively sticky; keep the dough soft.

title: Apple Pie Tortilla Turnovers
description: Warm cinnamon-spiced apples wrapped in flour tortillas, baked until golden, and finished with a crunchy cinnamon-sugar topping.
ingredients:
INGREDIENTS — APPLE FILLING
• Butter — 30 g | 2 tbsp
• Granny Smith apples, peeled and diced — 300 g | about 2½ UK cups | about 2½ US cups
• Braeburn apples, peeled and diced — 300 g | about 2½ UK cups | about 2½ US cups
• Light brown sugar — 60 g | 4 tbsp | n UK cup | n US cup
• Ground cinnamon — 4 g | 2 tsp | n tbsp
• Ground nutmeg — 0.5 g | ¼ tsp

• Lemon juice — 15 ml | 1 tbsp | 3 tsp

INGREDIENTS — ASSEMBLY

title: Peanut Butter Sandwich Cookies
description: with Creamy Peanut Butter Filling Soft, rich peanut butter cookies sandwiched around a smooth peanut butter filling.
ingredients:
• 1 cup unsalted butter, melted
• 1 cup granulated sugar
• 1 cup natural creamy peanut butter, no added sugar, made with just peanuts and salt
• 2 large eggs
• 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
• 2 cups all-purpose flour
• 2 tablespoons cornstarch
• 1 teaspoon baking soda
• 1 teaspoon baking powder
INGREDIENTS — FILLING
• ½ cup natural creamy peanut butter, no added sugar
• 1 cup powdered sugar
• 4 to 5 tablespoons milk of your choice
• 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
directions:
1. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, mix the melted butter and granulated sugar. Stir in the 1 cup peanut butter, eggs, and 2
teaspoons vanilla until smooth.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking soda, and baking powder. Add the dry ingredients
to the wet mixture and stir just until combined.
4. Scoop the dough into evenly sized portions and place them on the prepared baking sheets, leaving room to
spread. Gently flatten each portion.
5. Bake for about 9–12 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers look just done. Ovens vary, so check early.

6. For the filling, mix the ½ cup peanut butter, powdered sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Add milk 1 tablespoon at a

title: Extra-Crispy Homemade Potato Fries
description: A homemade potato snack made with russet potatoes, potato starch, and dehydrated potato flakes for a crispier finish.
ingredients:

• ¼ cup water

directions:
1. Peel the potatoes if desired, then grate or finely shred them. Squeeze out as much excess moisture as
possible.

mixing until the mixture holds together; use only as much as needed.
3. Season with salt. Shape the mixture into fries, patties, or small potato bites, as desired.
4. Heat oil in a deep, heavy pot or fryer. Carefully fry in small batches until golden and crisp, making sure

before disposing of it safely.

title: Sourdough Bread Starter & Bread
description: A traditional potato-flake starter with a slow overnight bread rise DESCRIPTION A sweet, potato-flake sourdough-style starter is maintained by regular feedings and used to make a slow-rising, homemade loaf. This recipe makes approximately 2–3 loaves, depending on pan size. SOURDOUGH BREAD STARTER
ingredients:
Starter
3/4 c. sugar
3 Tbsp. instant potato flakes
2 pkg. dry yeast
1 c. warm water (110°)

Bread
1/2 c. oil
1 1/2 c. warm water (110° to 115°)
1 c. Starter (at room temperature)
6 c. bread flour (make only with bread flour)
1/8 to 1/3 c. sugar
1 Tbsp. salt
directions:
Starter

1. Mix all ingredients well. Put in a jar or container with lid on loosely and let stand at room temperature for 2 to 3 days.
2. Then put in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days.
3. Take out and “feed” with the same ingredients, except yeast. Let stand all day or overnight.
4. Use 1 cup of Starter in bread and store 1 cup of Starter in the refrigerator. Every 5 to 7 days “feed” as directed. Keep in
refrigerator until convenient time to make bread.
5. Starter may be given to a friend who wishes to make Sourdough Bread. Measure 1 cup to give away.
6. If, after 3 “feedings” you have not made bread, throw away a cup of Starter. More than 3 cups does not keep well.

SOURDOUGH BREAD
1. In a large bowl make a stiff batter of the above ingredients.
2. Grease a large bowl. Put dough in and turn over so the oily side is on top. Cover lightly with foil and let stand overnight. Do
not refrigerate dough.
3. In morning (8 to 12 hours) punch dough down. Knead a few times (10 to 12 tours) until air is released.
4. Divide dough into 2 to 3 parts, depending on size of pan (pan should be 1/3 full of dough). Put oil on top. Cover with
waxed paper and let rise 8 to 10 hours or all day, depending on temperature of room. Dough rises very slowly.

may be frozen or refrigerated.

title: Homemade Pizza Dough
description: A soft, versatile yeast dough for making 4 large homemade pizza crusts.
ingredients:
• 4 cups warm water
• 2 tablespoons yeast
• 2 tablespoons sugar or honey
• ½ cup oil
• ½ cup plus 2 tablespoons milk powder
• 10 cups flour
• 5 tablespoons vital wheat gluten
• 1 tablespoon salt
directions:
1. In a very large mixing bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and sugar or honey. Let stand for 5–10 minutes, until foamy if
using active dry yeast. If using instant yeast, you can continue after mixing.
2. Stir in the oil and milk powder.
3. Add the flour, vital wheat gluten, and salt. Mix until a rough dough forms. Add the flour gradually and adjust as needed; the
dough should be soft and workable.
4. Knead for 8–10 minutes in a mixer or about 10–12 minutes by hand, until smooth and elastic.
5. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for about 45–75 minutes, or until doubled in size.
6. Gently deflate the dough and divide it into 4 equal portions for 4 large pizza crusts.
7. Shape or stretch each portion into a large pizza crust. If the dough springs back, cover it and let it rest for 10–15 minutes,
then shape again.
8. Add sauce and toppings. Bake on a preheated pizza stone or baking sheet at 450–500°F (230–260°C) until the crust is
browned and the toppings are cooked, usually about 10–15 minutes depending on crust thickness, oven, and toppings.
notes:
• Use warm, not hot, water so the yeast works properly.
• For a crisper crust, preheat the oven and baking surface thoroughly before adding the pizza.
• If not using all the dough right away, divide it, lightly oil each portion, cover, and refrigerate for up to 24–48 hours. Bring it
toward room temperature before shaping.
• This is a large batch; use a large bowl or mix in batches if your mixer cannot safely handle it.

Approximate dough-only nutrition per crust (¼ of the batch): 1,150–1,350 calories, 30–38 g protein, 220–260 g carbohydrates,
and 18–25 g fat. Estimates vary with flour type, oil, and actual dough yield. Sauce and toppings are not included.

title: Scottish Rumbledethumps
description: A traditional Scottish comfort dish of mashed potatoes and cabbage, finished with cheddar and baked until golden.
ingredients:
• 2 lb (900 g) potatoes, peeled and chopped
• ½ medium cabbage, shredded
• 1 medium onion, sliced (optional)
• 3 tbsp butter, plus extra for greasing
• ½ cup (125 mL) shredded sharp cheddar cheese
• ¼ cup (60 mL) milk, approximately
• Salt and black pepper to taste
directions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a medium ovenproof baking dish with butter.
2. Place the potatoes in a pot of salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 15–20 minutes, or until fork-tender. Drain well.
3. Meanwhile, cook the shredded cabbage and optional sliced onion in a little boiling water for about 5–8 minutes, until tender.

4. Mash the potatoes with the 3 tbsp butter and enough milk to make them smooth but still firm. Season with salt and black

title: Homemade Cinnamon Rolls
description: Soft, fluffy yeast rolls swirled with buttery brown sugar and cinnamon—a comforting homemade treat.
times: Yield Prep time Rise time Oven About 12 rolls 25 minutes About 1½–2 hours 350°F (175°C)

title: Homemade Dinner Rolls
description: Soft, tender, buttery dinner rolls with a lightly sweet flavour—perfect for family meals and holiday dinners.
ingredients:
• 1 cup milk (250 ml), room temperature
• 1 egg
• 2¼ teaspoons instant yeast (7 g)
• ¼ cup sugar (50 g)
• 3¼ cups all-purpose flour (406 g)
• 1 teaspoon salt (5 g)
• ¼ cup softened butter (50 g)
directions:
1. Combine the ingredients. In a large bowl, mix the room-temperature milk, egg, instant yeast, and sugar. Add the flour and
salt, then mix until a rough dough forms.
2. Knead and add the butter. Knead for 3–4 minutes, then add the softened butter a little at a time. Continue kneading for
8–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and soft. It may feel slightly tacky; add flour sparingly if needed.
3. First rise. Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for about 60–90 minutes, or until
doubled in size.
4. Shape the rolls. Gently press the air from the dough. Divide into 16 equal pieces and shape each into a smooth ball. Place
in a greased 9 × 13-inch pan or on a lined baking sheet, leaving a little space between them.
5. Second rise. Cover and let rise for 30–45 minutes, until puffy.
6. Bake. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake for 18–22 minutes, until the rolls are golden on top and cooked through.
7. Finish and cool. If desired, brush the hot rolls with a little extra butter (not included in the ingredient list). Let rest for a few
minutes before serving.
notes:
• Add the softened butter after the dough first comes together; this helps the flour hydrate and makes kneading easier.
• Dough should be soft and slightly tacky, not dry. Too much extra flour can make rolls heavy.
• For evenly sized rolls, weigh the dough and divide the total weight by 16.
• If the tops brown too quickly, loosely cover with foil near the end of baking.

title: Strawberry Turnovers
description: Flaky puff pastry filled with sweet, lightly tangy strawberries, baked until golden and finished with an optional vanilla icing. Yield Prep time Bake time Oven About 6–8 turnovers 20 minutes 18–25 minutes 400°F (200°C) Ingredients — Turnovers • 1 package puff pastry (about 450 g), thawed • 1 cup chopped strawberries • ¼ cup granulated sugar • 1 tablespoon cornstarch • 1 teaspoon lemon juice • 1 egg, beaten Ingredients — Optional Vanilla Icing • ½ cup icing sugar • 1–2 teaspoons milk • ¼ teaspoon vanilla extract
ingredients:
Strawberry Turnovers
Flaky puff pastry filled with sweet, lightly tangy strawberries, baked until golden and finished with an optional vanilla icing.
Yield Prep time Bake time Oven
About 6–8 turnovers 20 minutes 18–25 minutes 400°F (200°C)
Ingredients — Turnovers
• 1 package puff pastry (about 450 g), thawed
• 1 cup chopped strawberries

• 1 tablespoon cornstarch
• 1 teaspoon lemon juice
• 1 egg, beaten
Ingredients — Optional Vanilla Icing
• ½ cup icing sugar

Directions
1. Heat the oven. Preheat to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Make the filling. In a small bowl, combine the chopped strawberries, granulated sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice. Stir
gently until evenly mixed.
3. Prepare the pastry. Unfold the thawed puff pastry on a lightly floured surface. Cut into 6–8 equal squares, depending on
the size you prefer.
4. Fill. Spoon a small amount of strawberry filling onto one side of each square, leaving the edges clear. Avoid adding too
much liquid from the bottom of the bowl.
5. Fold and seal. Fold each square diagonally to form a triangle. Press the edges together with a fork. Transfer to the lined
baking sheet and cut a small vent in the top of each turnover.
6. Add egg wash. Brush the tops with the beaten egg, taking care not to let it pool around the cut edges.
7. Bake. Bake for 18–25 minutes, until puffed and deep golden. Cool on the baking sheet for several minutes, then move to a
rack.
8. Make the icing (optional). Stir the icing sugar, 1 teaspoon milk, and vanilla together. Add more milk a few drops at a time
until it is drizzle-ready. Drizzle over cooled turnovers.
Grandma’s Tips

• If the strawberries are very juicy, let the filling sit briefly and spoon mostly fruit into the pastry so the edges seal well.
• Chill assembled turnovers for 10 minutes before baking if the pastry has softened.
• Let turnovers cool before icing so the icing does not melt straight off. The filling will be very hot just after baking.

Approximate per turnover, assuming 8 turnovers and including a modest amount of optional icing: 250–330 calories; 3–5 g protein; 30–40 g
carbohydrates; 12–18 g fat. Values vary by puff pastry brand, turnover size, and whether icing is used.

title: Sweet Red Pepper & Jalapeño Jelly
description: A bright, sweet-and-tangy pepper jelly with a gentle-to-fiery jalapeño kick. DESCRIPTION A glossy homemade jelly that pairs sweet red bell peppers with fresh jalapeños. Serve with crackers and cream cheese, alongside roasted meats, or as a condiment for sandwiches.
ingredients:
• 3 cups chopped sweet red bell peppers, seeds removed
• 1 cup finely chopped fresh hot jalapeño peppers, seeds removed
• 1 cup clear apple cider vinegar with 5% acidity
• 5 cups pure white granulated cane sugar
• 1 box liquid fruit pectin (2 pouches; 3 ounces total)
• 1 teaspoon natural unsalted butter, to reduce excess foam during boiling
• 1 teaspoon sea salt, to balance the sweet and tangy flavors
directions:
1. Prepare: Wash peppers. Remove stems and seeds, then chop the red bell peppers and finely chop the jalapeños. For less
heat, remove the jalapeño membranes as well. Wear gloves when handling hot peppers and avoid touching your eyes.
2. Combine: In a large, deep stainless-steel pot, combine the chopped peppers, vinegar, sugar, butter, and salt. Stir well.
3. Boil: Bring the mixture to a full rolling boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently so the sugar dissolves and the mixture
does not scorch.
4. Add pectin: Add the liquid fruit pectin according to the package directions. Return to a full rolling boil and boil for the time
specified by the pectin manufacturer, stirring constantly.
5. Check and skim: Remove from the heat. Skim off any remaining foam with a clean spoon.
6. Fill jars: Ladle the hot jelly into clean, hot canning jars, leaving the headspace specified by a tested recipe for this exact pectin
and batch. Wipe rims, apply lids, and process in a boiling-water canner only using a tested recipe and processing time
appropriate for your jar size and altitude.
7. Cool and store: Let processed jars cool undisturbed for 12–24 hours. Check seals. Refrigerate any unsealed jars and use
them promptly. Label sealed jars with the date.
CATEGORIES
Condiments • Preserves • Pepper Jelly • Sweet & Spicy • Canning
notes:
• Chop the peppers evenly for a more consistent texture.
• Adjust the heat by removing jalapeño membranes; keep the seeds removed as listed.
• Use only vinegar labeled 5% acidity and the exact type/amount of pectin specified by the recipe package.
• For shelf-stable storage, use a tested canning recipe and its exact processing instructions. Do not guess the water-bath
processing time or rely on an inverted-jar method.
NUTRITION (ESTIMATE)
Nutrition depends on the final yield and serving size. The recipe contains 5 cups of sugar, so it is a high-sugar preserve. Per 1
tablespoon, a rough estimate is about 40–50 calories and 10–12 g carbohydrate, with negligible fat and protein. This estimate is
approximate and is not a laboratory analysis.
Food-safety note: The ingredient list alone does not establish a safe shelf-stable canning process. Use a reputable, tested pepper-jelly canning
recipe that matches these ingredients and the pectin product, or refrigerate/freeze the jelly using suitable containers.

title: Sourdough Pizza Crust Recipe
description: Amy Duska A no-fuss sourdough pizza crust recipe that's crispy, chewy and perfectly charred on top and bottom. An easy overnight dough that holds all your favorite toppings and bakes to perfection every time!
ingredients:
Sourdough pizza crust
100 g (1/3 cup) sourdough starter discard if you would like to use active starter reduce to ¼ cup
(50 g
10 g (2 teaspoons) fi ne sea salt see notes if using a different type of salt
30 g (2 tablespoons) olive oil
50 g (1/3 cup + 1 tablespoon) whole wheat fl our
450 g (3 3/4 cups ) all-purpose fl our bread fl our or 00 fl our can be used, see notes
325 g (1 1/3 cups + 1 teaspoon) water see notes

your choice of toppings
directions:
How to Make Sourdough Pizza in a Cast Iron Skillet
1. The night before you want to bake: Add 100 g sourdough starter discard , 10 g fi ne sea salt , 30 g
olive oil , 50 g whole wheat fl our , 450 g all-purpose fl our , and 325 g water to a large mixing bowl
and mix by hand until fully combined. Cover and let the dough ferment at room temperature
overnight.
2. The next morning: Perform a set of stretch and folds to strengthen the dough. Wet your hand
with water to prevent sticking. While keeping the dough in the bowl, gently pull one side up and
fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat on all sides until you've completed a full circle.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for 8 to 36 hours. The dough can be used immediately to make
your pizza, but the cold ferment is optional and will help develop more fl avor.
3. When ready to cook: Remove the dough from the fridge and let it rest on the counter for 30
minutes at room temperature. Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Shape each portion into a
ball on a generously fl oured work surface. Cover the dough with a tea towel and let them rest for
30 minutes.
4. Turn on your oven's broiler to HIGH. On a stovetop heat a cast iron skillet over medium to
medium-high heat. If needed, lightly oil the cast iron skillet to prevent sticking.
5. While the skillet is preheating, press a dough ball into an 8" circle on a fl oured surface using your
hands. Use more fl our as needed to prevent sticking. (If the dough is di ffi cult to shape, let it rest
for 15 minutes on the counter to allow the gluten to relax.)
6 . When the skillet is hot, lay the circle of dough in it. VERY carefully use your fi ngers to press the
edges of the dough to cover the bottom of the skillet. Immediately add the sauce and toppings to
the crust and cook for 5-6 minutes or until the bottom of the crust starts to char.
TIP: If the dough is too thick, you will need to cook it longer on the stovetop at a lower
temperature to ensure the crust cooks through properly. You can also try putting it under the
broiler for a few minutes before adding the toppings to help it cook through and avoid the "gum
line" in the center.
7. Once the bottom has turned brown and charred, transfer the cast iron skillet to the broiler to
fi nish baking the top of the pizza for 2-4 minutes. Remove from the oven, slice, and serve hot.
Make sure to keep an eye on it to prevent the toppings from burning, as broiler temperatures can
vary. Every oven is different, so individual results may vary.
How to Bake Sourdough Pizza on A Pizza Stone
1. Place the pizza stone in a cold oven and preheat it to 450°F (232°C) Press the dough into a crust
and add your desired toppings. (The dough can be divided into 4 personal-sized pizzas or 2 larger
pizzas.)
2. Once the oven and pizza stone are heated, carefully use a pizza peel to transfer the dough
directly onto the pizza stone. Be sure to move quickly to avoid the dough from losing its shape.
Alternatively, you can shape the pizza on a piece of parchment paper and then transfer it to the
baking stone.
3. Bake the pizza for 15-20 minutes or until the toppings are done and the crust is cooked through.
nutrition:
Serving: 1(8") crust Calories: 541kcal Carbohydrates: 100g
Protein: 14g Fat: 9g
notes:
Measuring Ingredients: Our recipes use a kitchen scale for precise measurements when
developing our recipes. Measuring cups can lead to inconsistent results, so keep that in mind if
you ’ re not using a scale.
Flour: All-purpose fl our can be substituted with bread fl our or 00 fl our. If you make this switch,
you may need to adjust the hydration level slightly, as bread fl our and 00 fl our absorb water
differently than all-purpose fl our. Add a little more or less water as needed to achieve the right
dough consistency.
Adjusting Hydration: We ’ ve adjusted the recipe to 70% hydration for easier handling. If the dough
feels too sticky, reduce the water by 25 grams next time. If it feels too stiff, add 25 grams.
Adjusting salt: We use Redmonds fi ne sea salt weighing 10 grams per 2 teaspoons. If using
regular table salt, use 1 ½ teaspoons. If using fl aky sea salt, use a heaping 2 ½ teaspoons.
How to Store and Reheat: Store leftover pizza in a closed container in the fridge for up to 5 days.
Reheat leftover pizza in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for about 10 minutes, or until heated
through and crispy. For a quicker option, microwave on a plate for 30-60 seconds, though the
crust may be softer.
How to Freeze Unbaked Pizza Dough: After the second rise in the fridge, divide the dough into 2
or 4 balls and coat them with oil to prevent sticking. Place each one in a freezer bag, removing
excess air. Store in the freezer for up to 3 months. To use, thaw in the refrigerator for 12 hours or
overnight. Let the dough come to room temperature before shaping and baking as directed.
How to Freeze Baked Pizza Crust: After the fi nal rise in the fridge, shape the dough and cook in
a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes. Finish under the broiler for 1-2 minutes.
Let cool, then freeze in a freezer-safe bag with parchment paper between each crust. To bake,
preheat the oven to 400°F (204°C). Place the frozen crust on a baking sheet (no need to thaw),
add toppings, and bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and cooked through.
